headline: Computational methods resolve spatial gene expression to cell and tissue architecture
label: Spatial Transcriptomics Computational Methods
summary: Models now link spatial transcriptomics to morphology, cell-level resolution, and spatial statistics, extending scRNA-seq frameworks to tissue context.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational recovery of cellular and tissue organization from spatial transcriptomics, where expression is modeled jointly with histology, morphology, or spatial geometry. DeSpaST deconvolves spot-level data to cell resolution using histology and a graph, STRESS refines expression onto finer grids via 3D state-space modeling, and Tera-MIND conditions diffusion-based simulation of teravoxel mouse brains on spatial expression. CSS predicts cell size from gene expression, linking transcriptomes to morphology. Statistical frameworks extend this direction: netPCF generalizes pair correlation functions to network-embedded domains, GESSO performs graph-regularized gene set scoring, stGP decomposes multi-sample spatiotemporal programs, and a senescence study applies Ripley's functions. Garfield and TopoMetry address integration and latent geometry in single-cell data. The set is heterogeneous; the novelty lies in spatially aware, geometry- and morphology-informed models rather than expression-only annotation.
